newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Premiere sees growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Premiere sees growth in 1997.

text.p: German pay television channel Premiere said on Wednesday that it reached break even in 1996 and boasted a 30 percent rise in turnover to 500 million marks.

Looking ahead to the new year, the company said in a statement it expected operating profit in "double-digit millions" after adjusting for a planned 100 million-mark investment to acquire subscribers.
Premiere is jointly owned by media group Bertelsmann and French pay TV giant Canal Plus, each with 37.5 percent, and Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch, who owns 25 percent.
The pay TV channel said it now has around 1.4 million subscribers and that in the past six weeks 100,000 new subscribers came on board.

The company pointed out that during the same period its new competitor, Kirch's digital pay TV channel DF1, had fallen far short of its envisaged goal of gaining 200,000 subscribers by the end of the year.
"This development shows clearly that the programme offering of Premiere stands up in competition to the digital platform of DF1," it said.
